quiz.title: Class 12 Three-Dimensional Geometry Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on direction cosines and ratios, equations of lines and planes, angles, distances and coplanarity. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The direction cosines l, m, n of any line satisfy which relation?
questions.explanation: Direction cosines are the cosines of the angles a line makes with the axes, and they always satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1.

questions.q: A line has direction ratios 2, -1, 2. Its direction cosines are:
questions.explanation: Divide each ratio by the magnitude √(4+1+4) = 3, giving direction cosines 2/3, -1/3, 2/3.

questions.q: The angle between two lines with direction ratios (1, 2, 2) and (2, 2, 1) is:
Two lines with direction ratios (a₁, b₁, c₁) and (a₂, b₂, c₂) are perpendicular when:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines have a zero dot product of their direction ratios: a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0. Equal ratios instead mean the lines are parallel.

questions.q: The plane 2x - 3y + 6z = 7 has which vector normal to it?
questions.explanation: For a plane ax + by + cz = d, the coefficients give the normal vector, so here the normal is 2i - 3j + 6k.

questions.q: The distance of the point (1, 2, 3) from the plane 2x - 2y + z + 3 = 0 is:
The angle between a line with direction ratios (1, 1, 2) and a plane with normal (2, -1, 1) is found using:
questions.explanation: For a line and a plane the angle uses the sine, since θ is measured from the plane while the dot product gives the angle with the normal: sinθ = |b·n|/(|b||n|).

questions.q: Two lines are coplanar if and only if:
options: the shortest distance between them is zero
questions.explanation: Coplanar lines lie in one plane, so the shortest distance between them is zero (skew lines have a non-zero shortest distance).

faq.q: What topics does the Class 12 Three-Dimensional Geometry chapter cover?
faq.a: It covers direction cosines and direction ratios of a line, the vector and Cartesian equations of a line, the angle between two lines, coplanarity, the equation of a plane in various forms, the angle between two planes and between a line and a plane, and the distance of a point from a plane.

faq.q: What is the difference between direction cosines and direction ratios?
faq.a: Direction cosines are the cosines of the angles a line makes with the x, y and z axes and always satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1. Direction ratios are any numbers proportional to the direction cosines, so a line has one set of direction cosines but infinitely many sets of direction ratios.

faq.q: How do you find the angle between a line and a plane?
faq.a: Use the direction ratios of the line and the normal to the plane. Since the angle is measured from the plane and not its normal, it is given by sinθ = |b·n| / (|b||n|), where b is the line's direction vector and n is the plane's normal.

faq.q: How do you check whether two lines are coplanar?
faq.a: Two lines are coplanar when the shortest distance between them is zero. In practice you check that the vector joining a point on each line, together with the two direction vectors, gives a zero scalar triple product. If it is non-zero the lines are skew.
